headline: Sanofi's $41 billion cash deal for Insmed leads the deal flow, while markets try to hold Monday's Nvidia-led rally after Jensen Huang's return as CEO. Anthropic's shares slipped below their $83 IPO price in premarket trading, and private credit ratings are under growing scrutiny.

paragraphs.text: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $41 billion in cash, the largest pharma deal of the year and, per MarketWatch, the biggest biotech deal in nearly three years. Endpoints calls it the first biopharma megadeal since Pfizer's $43 billion takeover of Seagen. The logic, per the FT and others, is to replace revenue from Dupixent, whose patent cliff is approaching. STAT says Sanofi gets two approved lung disease medicines. Fierce Biotech counts three commercial and late-phase respiratory assets. Coverage differs on the count, so the exact pipeline contribution is worth checking in the deal documents. MedWatch says the deal followed weeks of takeover rumors. TipRanks reports Sanofi shares rose and Insmed stock jumped. For a dealmaker, an all-cash deal of this size shows big pharma will pay up for commercial-stage assets rather than wait for earlier-stage science.

paragraphs.text: The same Dupixent story has another side. Kymera's oral eczema drug met its goals in a 244-patient mid-stage trial. Analysts quoted by BioPharma Dive and Fierce Biotech described the efficacy as comparable to an injectable biologic and said it could challenge Dupixent, the Sanofi-Regeneron franchise. Phase 2 data are early, but they show why Sanofi is shopping.

paragraphs.text: Elsewhere in deals and financings, Lilly bought Huntington's disease developer LoQus23 in a deal worth up to $725 million. STAT's Pharmalittle counts it as Lilly's 15th acquisition of 2026. The WSJ reports Bayer will pay more attention to midstage assets in its next pharma deals, a shift from its recent early-stage focus. Venture money is still flowing: Ritzey, led by the founders of Intra-Cellular, debuted with $112 million, and Avenzo began trading on Nasdaq after a reverse merger. A House select committee report warns that US biotech is being hollowed out as China gains ground, and it will feed the policy debate over China in-licensing.

paragraphs.text: On the regulatory front, the FDA approved BridgeBio's drug for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, the first approved treatment for the condition and the first of three approvals the company hopes for. STAT says it could reach $1 billion a year in sales. Capricor said it will appeal the FDA's Friday rejection of its Duchenne cell therapy and disputes the agency's data integrity concerns. Roche won a second FDA approval for its oral breast cancer drug giredestrant, this time in early-stage disease, a much larger market. Roche says it could be the best-selling drug ever, which is a company claim. Arcus stopped a Phase 3 pancreatic cancer trial of its CD73 inhibitor. Savara shares fell after the FDA missed a decision date, and analysts suggested agency capacity problems.

paragraphs.text: Policy and payer news was heavy. CMS published final negotiated prices for 13 drugs in the third Medicare round, including Lilly's Trulicity and Gilead's Biktarvy, with estimated savings of $9.2 billion. A proposed CMS rule would cut roughly $100 billion over a decade from Medicare Advantage star-ratings payments. One analyst called it almost overwhelming in scope, and litigation looks all but certain, which matters for insurer earnings. Tampa General lost its 340B lawsuit against Lilly, a sign of rising tension between hospitals and drugmakers. Florida sued the Leapfrog Group over its hospital safety grades. WTW's survey projects global health insurance costs up 10.2% next year, a second straight double-digit increase.

paragraphs.text: Monday's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO drove a rally. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had their best sessions since April 2025, per CNBC and the NYT. The FT says Nvidia added nearly $1 trillion in value, and MarketWatch cites a strategist saying retail buyers from last week made an average gain of 11% on Monday. Analysts scrambled to upgrade the stock, and some strategists told CNBC the move could mark a bottom for the AI sell-off, with spending and data-center risks still in view. HPE raised its forecast on strong AI demand but its stock sank, a reminder that good AI numbers are not guaranteed to be rewarded.

paragraphs.text: Today the tone is cooler. Nasdaq futures fell and the FT says US tech is set to slip after the surge. Nomura argues forced, mechanical buying added to Monday's momentum, which suggests part of the rally was positioning rather than conviction. RBC's derivatives strategist thinks the VIX is still inflated and expects more whiplash. FT Alphaville notes leveraged short-Nvidia ETFs blew up. Julius Baer calls the earlier AI sell-off a realignment of expectations, not a broken investment cycle, while Bank of America's Michael Hartnett remains risk-off until global rate hikes fade next spring.

paragraphs.text: Washington is part of the story. The FT reports Silicon Valley figures lobbied Trump and JD Vance to bring Huang back, and the NYT says the move sidelined national security concerns. The FT estimates Trump made up to $15 million on Nvidia shares, based on the maximum holding in his latest disclosure. Separately, the administration sanctioned Singapore-based Megaspeed, and lawmakers released documents showing Commerce had approved sales of more than 800,000 AI chips to Chinese firms, some tied to the military. Governance and political risk are now live issues for anyone holding the AI trade.

paragraphs.text: On macro, the Fed's John Williams said higher rates are likely over time to address inflation, and expects inflation to move closer to 2% in 2027. The FT reports the Fed's Michelle Bowman is being probed over whether she breached the blackout period. Ebury says the dollar is now closely tied to AI-trade sentiment. The DXY dropped after reaching a 20-month high. German business sentiment improved again, and surveys show Germany growing at its fastest in over four years while France struggles. Singapore's economy is on track for its strongest year since 2011, excluding 2021, helped by AI.

paragraphs.text: In commodities, oil fell on supply-surplus expectations weighed against Middle East shipping risk, and European gas slipped but stays elevated on cold weather and low storage. China extended its pause on some critical-material export curbs to the US until January, days after the Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen. The FT says traders are shipping US copper to China as tariff fears ease. The LME is speeding up listing for metal from new plants, and German industrial groups launched a rare-earths trading house. Bloomberg notes grocery prices are rising even as gasoline eases.

paragraphs.text: Private credit's plumbing is under scrutiny. KBRA revised its outlook on Goldman Sachs BDC to negative, though the list gives no reasoning, so the cause is unclear. Egan-Jones is defending its private credit ratings. Its president told the FT the firm is the Tesla of ratings, able to produce thousands of scores because of its technology investment. That is a self-description from a small agency, and it sits awkwardly beside the growing role of such ratings in the asset class. Taken together, the stories point to closer attention on both credit quality and who is doing the rating.

paragraphs.text: Bloomberg profiles Hamza Lemssouguer's unwind of positions. He was one of Europe's most successful credit traders, betting on the riskiest borrowers, often through complex derivatives, and the story offers a look at how such bets work. Commerzbank is reportedly weighing a partial retreat from US Treasury trading, including leaving the repo market or partnering with a broker-dealer, ahead of new Treasury clearing requirements. If other banks follow, that could matter for market liquidity, though the report describes only options under consideration.

paragraphs.text: On the fundraising and lending side, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners closed its first CFO at 1.7 billion euros. The list doesn't spell out the acronym, but it is presumably a structured vehicle. Monroe Capital provided financing support for Waveborn's acquisition of Jake Rosen Entertainment, with no terms disclosed. Deloitte warns Ghana's 2027 budget borrowing could squeeze private credit, which appears to mean lending to the private sector, though the report is thinly detailed. Distress shows at the edges: robot startup Foundation, backed by Eric Trump, is seeking an emergency bridge loan and has cut employee health benefits while it awaits a $150 million investment from Korea's Base Group. FT Alphaville also flags a SpaceX bond hangover, but the headline gives no detail.

paragraphs.text: Beyond Sanofi, the other large deal is in cybersecurity: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in a $44 billion transaction, per the NYT, as AI-driven hacking worries weigh on companies and governments. At the DealBook Summit, Skydance CEO David Ellison confirmed Elon Musk invested in the company formed by the $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Two jumbo deals in a day suggest strategic buyers have both appetite and financing.

paragraphs.text: The Anthropic IPO is the equity-market story. Shares fell below the $83 IPO price in premarket trading, per Bloomberg, Reuters and others, wiping out gains from a record-setting debut. Reuters says the debut rally has unraveled. Premarket moves are thin, and regular trading may differ, but a broken IPO tends to affect how the next AI issuer prices. Elsewhere, Compass Group plans to move its primary listing to the US, adding to worries about London's public markets. The FT says groups are chasing liquidity and valuation, and its columnists argue London needs a stronger pipeline of listings. Ousted BP chair Albert Manifold is set to join Aggreko's board after its IPO, and he denies bullying allegations, calling them lies. Egypt's Misr Life Insurance plans to raise up to $185 million from a listing.

Dongwon says a possible StarKist sale remains undecided as the group weighs M&A options. Centre Lane is targeting $1 billion for Fund VI, focused on complex mid-market situations. Actuate Energy, backed by NGP, will invest $327 million with Sungrow in Spain's largest battery storage portfolio. In banking, First Horizon's CEO said the bank wants to stay positioned to be a buyer or seller as consolidation continues. Payoneer won conditional OCC approval for a trust bank charter, and insurance startup Corgi applied for a national bank charter.
